author: William MacAskill & Fin Moorhouse (Forethought)
title: Preparing for the Intelligence Explosion
central_scenario_summary: AI that can substitute for human research labour likely arrives within one to two decades and grows in collective capability hundreds of times faster than the human research workforce, driving a 'century in a decade' of technological progress and then an 'industrial explosion' as AI plus robots remove human labour as the bottleneck to physical production. This creates rapid-fire 'grand challenges' — including AI takeover, destructive technologies, and extreme concentration of economic and political power — alongside potential radical abundance; institutions are too slow by default, so preparation must start now.

quotes.text: There's now a serious chance we will see AI far smarter than humans within the coming decade.
AI that can accelerate research could drive a century of technological progress over just a few years.

capability_pace.notes: Explicit intelligence-explosion scenario: ~even chance of a software feedback loop; AI research effort growing >=300x faster than human research effort even in the conservative case.

quotes.text: if human-level AI and dextrous robots can substitute for almost all skilled human labour, things would be very different
it would become increasingly hard for anyone else to claw back relative influence through hard work

expertise_erosion.notes: Human expertise loses its scarcity value through replacement: returns to skill and effort collapse relative to returns on capital and land ownership.

quotes.text: we might expect a century's worth of technological progress to more than double average incomes; abundant AI and robotic labour from an industrial explosion could dramatically increase that again
we think a century of technological progress in a decade — or far more — is more likely than not

productivity_breadth.notes: Acceleration is asymmetric (simulation-heavy fields faster than experiment-bound ones) but economy-wide and transformative overall.

quotes.text: The main bottleneck to rapid industrial growth — human labour — melts away.
AI systems render human participation increasingly unnecessary for functioning governments, cultures, and economies

substitution.notes: Historically machines complemented labour; the paper's core claim is that AI plus robotics ends that complementarity.

quotes.text: An intelligence explosion could cause huge gains in material wealth and income... with the potential for thousands of AI and robot assistants per person, if people choose to have that

demand_absorption.notes: Envisages vast new consumption (personalised culture, services, assistants) absorbing output; but this is about consumption possibilities, not labor demand — the paper does not claim new human jobs absorb displaced workers.

quotes.text: the world will need to handle these challenges fast, on a timescale far shorter than what human institutions are designed for
it's hard to speed up humans themselves, and their interactions, thoughts, and learning

mobility_adjustment.notes: The paper is about institutional/decision-making adjustment rather than occupational reallocation specifically; scored 0 because its central mechanism is that human adaptation cannot keep pace with the shock.

quotes.text: AI-driven explosive growth could result in an even smaller fraction of people (or companies, or countries) holding an even larger fraction of wealth.
If the labour share shrinks significantly, then without redistribution most income would come from rents on capital and land

rent_concentration.notes: First-mover advantages could make leads permanent; in the extreme, 'almost all global power could be concentrated into one place.' Redistribution is flagged as the counterweight.

quotes.text: There's now a serious chance we will see AI far smarter than humans within the coming decade.
It seems likely to us that AI research effort will reach parity with human research labour within the next two decades

timeline_years.notes: Central economic impact (technology + industrial explosion) within roughly a decade of writing, with parity possibly 'in a matter of years' and up to two decades.

inequality_prediction.score: Radical abundance is possible — a century of progress could more than double average incomes and AI/robot labour could multiply that — but it is not guaranteed to be shared: if the labour share shrinks, income flows to owners of capital and land, wealth could concentrate 'in only a few hands,' and first movers could lock in permanent dominance, so preventing extreme, hard-to-reverse concentration of power requires deliberate institutions and redistribution.

quotes.text: an intelligence explosion could lead to huge gains in wealth which are concentrated in only a few hands
